summary: Publish a static build with no application server or database.

alternatives.why_not: Separate clients increase parallel implementation and testing work.

tradeoffs: Validate accessibility and platform-specific behavior separately.

backend.justification: Pre-rendered pages do not require a dynamic application API.

alternatives.why_not: Adds an API runtime for a static workload.

tradeoffs: Dynamic features require an API when introduced.

database.justification: Content is built into published assets.

alternatives.why_not: No mutable application records are required.

hosting.justification: Publish static assets without operating an application server.

alternatives.why_not: Adds a separate operations and infrastructure footprint.

tradeoffs: Check regional quotas, service coverage and availability targets.

supporting.justification: Keep builds portable and publish only approved artifacts.
tradeoffs: Maintain build reproducibility and dependency provenance.

breakdown.basis: Free-tier static hosting, conditional on fitting its limits and no paid add-ons.

assumptions: Planning allowances are heuristics. Size instances and confirm regional quotes before procurement.
Excludes taxes, engineering labor, payment transaction fees, separately metered SMS, and accelerator costs.
